title: Indian Startup Funding Falls 22% in a Week as AI Takes Half the Money
excerpt: Startups raised about $184 million (₹1,747 crore) across 17 deals between October 19 and 23, with two cheques — Even Healthcare and Different — accounting for more than half the total.
body:
• Indian startups raised over $184 million across 17 deals between October 19 and 23, down 22% from $236.2 million across 25 deals the week before.
  • AI startups took $93.9 million across six deals — 51% of the week's money — and healthtech took $60.6 million across two deals.
  • Two rounds did most of the work: Even Healthcare's $50 million Series B and AI startup Different's $48 million seed round total $98 million, over half the week.
  • Deal count fell 32% week on week, so the slowdown is fewer, more concentrated bets — not investors leaving the market.

Indian startup funding slowed sharply in the third week of October, even as artificial intelligence tightened its grip on the money that did move. Startups raised over $184 million — about ₹1,747 crore — across 17 deals between October 19 and 23, a 22 per cent fall from the $236.2 million raised the previous week, according to Inc42. The deal count fell 32 per cent, from 25 to 17.

Two cheques, more than half the week

The week's total was carried by two rounds. Even Healthcare raised a $50 million Series B, and Different, the AI startup founded by Ajeet Singh, raised a $48 million seed round. Together they account for $98 million — a little over half of everything raised. Strip them out and the remaining 15 deals raised about $86 million, according to the sector breakdown compiled by MalikTimes.

AI first, healthtech second, daylight third

AI startups raised $93.9 million across six deals, 51 per cent of the week's funding, with Different's seed round alone contributing more than half of the sector total. Healthtech followed with $60.6 million across two deals, anchored by Even Healthcare. AI and healthtech together took about 84 per cent of the money. Ecommerce, all of it direct-to-consumer brands, came third with $19.1 million across three deals, led by The Pant Project's $11.5 million Series B. Travel tech raised $6 million across two deals, including TravClan's $5 million, and food tech $3 million from Harajuku Tokyo Cafe's pre-Series A. Venture debt firm Trifecta Capital and early-stage investor Blume Ventures were the week's most active investors, backing two startups each.

What the pattern means

A 22 per cent weekly fall sounds like a retreat, but the composition tells a different story: capital is concentrating, not vanishing. When two rounds supply over half the total and two sectors take 84 per cent, investors are making fewer, larger, higher-conviction bets — a pattern that has defined Indian venture funding since the post-2021 correction. For founders outside AI and health, the message is that seed and early rounds are still closing, but at smaller sizes: the week's median deal outside the top two was in the low single-digit millions.

What to watch

Weekly funding totals are volatile — a single $100 million round can flip the trend in either direction, and the prior week's $236.2 million was itself up sharply on the week before it. The figure to watch is deal count: if it stays in the teens while AI keeps taking half the money, India's funding recovery will remain narrow, rewarding AI-adjacent founders and leaving consumer and fintech startups competing for a shrinking share of a concentrated pool.
